name: EU long-term resident's residence permit (zezwolenie na pobyt rezydenta długoterminowego UE)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 years of continuous, legal residence in Poland directly before the application. Time spent on an EU Blue Card counts fully; if held partly in another EU state, at least the final 2 years directly before the application must be in Poland.
requirements.fix_path: Continue accruing continuous legal residence; breaks under 6 months at a time (10 months total) are tolerated.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a stable, regular source of income sufficient to cover the applicant and any dependants.
requirements.fix_path: Document stable employment, business, or other regular income.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires valid health insurance (NFZ or private) covering costs in Poland.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm NFZ coverage through employment or purchase qualifying private insurance.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires confirmed knowledge of Polish, evidenced by a certificate, completion of Polish-language education, or a language exam -- this test is not required for plain permanent residence, making it the one requirement where the EU long-term route is stricter than pl_permanent_residence.
requirements.fix_path: Pass a recognised Polish-language exam (B1 is the commonly-required threshold in practice) or document Polish-language schooling.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' continuous legal residence
Proof of stable income and health insurance

outcome.duration_length: unlimited (residence card issued for 5 years, renewed as a card only)
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: grants EU-wide long-term resident mobility rights, distinct from Poland-only permanent residence

sources.title: Moduł Obsługi Spraw (mos.cudzoziemcy.gov.pl, Office for Foreigners' official case-handling portal) -- EU long-term resident permit conditions

Powroty.gov.pl (official Polish government portal, gov.pl domain) -- side-by-side comparison of permanent residence vs. EU long-term resident status, independent cross-check of the language and income conditions

Zielona Linia (Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy-run public information line) -- confirming the Blue Card cross-border portability provision and the 6-month/10-month continuity-break tolerances

notes: Genuinely distinct from pl_permanent_residence rather than a duplicate: both require 5 years and both are unlimited-duration outcomes, but EU long-term residence adds a confirmed Polish-language requirement that plain permanent residence does not carry, and in exchange grants EU-wide long-term-mobility rights (the ability to move long-term to certain other EU states under the 2003/109/EC directive) that plain Poland-only permanent residence does not. Poland is unusual among the countries built so far in offering these as two genuinely parallel, freestanding settled-category routes rather than one being a strict subset or later stage of the other -- an applicant chooses between them based on whether EU-wide mobility or a simpler no-language-test path matters more, confirmed via powroty.gov.pl's explicit side-by-side comparison of the two statuses. EU Blue Card holders get a specific acceleration on this route: time spent in another EU member state on that state's Blue Card counts toward the 5-year total, provided the final 2 years directly before the Polish application were spent in Poland on a Blue Card -- a cross-border portability feature confirmed via lexlege.pl's reproduction of the Act on Foreigners' Article on this point, and worth surfacing prominently on any comparison view since it rewards genuine EU-wide Blue Card mobility rather than penalising it.
